rule: ruling:sam-2026-10-07 claims 8, 10 and 11: the prototype wins by default and only a real constraint it cannot express overrides it; the real commodity reference list is far too large to ship with the page (repo-frontend-p5-009-m1), which overrides only where the results come from, not the as-you-type interaction, and DR1's row (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p5-005) judges a hint sentence, not this interaction, so it is no judgement on the same difference.
outcome: The prototype wins: with JavaScript, the commodity search behaves as DR2.1, listing results as you type with no Search press, ticking keeps the results open, Escape closes them, and a polite live region announces result and selection counts. The real constraint that the commodity reference list is too large to ship with the page overrides only where the results come from: they are fetched from the server's commodity catalogue rather than a list in the page. Without JavaScript the page keeps today's server-side Search button, its 3-character minimum and the server-rendered panel, so it still works.
